tagline: Ozark hill country, and a lake the CCC built.
intro: Highway AP twists for 24 miles through the Ozark hill country of the Mark Twain National Forest, through farmland and open pasture and up densely wooded hillsides of shortleaf pine and mixed hardwoods, with overlooks at Indian Creek and Blue Buck Knob. It ends where it meets Highway 14.

Off the road, the Ridge Runner Trail crosses limestone karst, over ground that runs from gently rolling to very steep, past rock outcrops and bluffs. It fords its creeks. None of the crossings has a bridge.

moments.title: Noblett Lake
moments.text: A Civilian Conservation Corps crew built this 26-acre lake during the Great Depression, and its picnic tables sit in the shade of sugar maples, shortleaf pines and oaks.

moments.title: Camp Willow
moments.text: The crew lived across the highway at Camp Willow, and what is left of it lies about 2.5 miles east of Highway AP on Forest Road 108, opposite the Noblett Lake road.

practical: There is no drinking water at the sites along the byway.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Blue Buck Knob National Forest Scenic Byway
